title: What is Igris?
description: Reliable execution for AI agents that can change real systems.
content: What is Igris? What you get The product lifecycle Who this is for Start here Honest claim boundaries # What is Igris? Igris is reliable execution for AI agents that can change real systems. Use it when an agent is about to do consequential work: touch infrastructure, call a payment API, mutate customer data, or otherwise change something outside the chat transcript. Direct model calls are still fine for ordinary prompting. Igris is for the actions that must survive failure, avoid blind retries, and remain inspectable after the fact. ## What you get - **Run consequential actions durably.** Submit an Action once with a business idempotency key and a bound contract. - **Recover from infrastructure failures.** If a runtime dies mid-flight, Igris can continue the managed run without you inventing a resume protocol. - **Stop when the outcome is uncertain.** When the external effect cannot be known safely, Igris fails closed and requires operator reconciliation instead of guessing. ## The product lifecycle text Action → Run → Recover → Reconcile when uncertain → Prove 1. **Action** — declare what the agent is allowed to do, as a typed contract bound to an executable target. 2. **Run** — submit one durable run with an explicit business idempotency key. 3. **Recover** — infrastructure failures are handled by the managed execution path; you wait and inspect, you do not manually poke checkpoints. 4. **Reconcile when uncertain** — unresolved external effects require an attributable operator assertion. 5. **Prove** — retrieve **Igris Run Proof**, a linked product view of distinct claims for that run. ## Who this is for Engineers building coding, infrastructure, and operational agents that have permission to change external systems. ## Start here | Step | Page | Outcome | |---:|---|---| | 1 | [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) | Install `igris-sdk`, configure endpoint and API key, understand the journey. | | 2 | [Your First Durable Action](/docs/first-durable-action) | Bind one Action, run it, wait, and inspect Igris Run Proof. | | 3 | [Actions](/docs/actions) | Learn the Action / binding / target model. | | 4 | [Igris Run Proof](/docs/igris-run-proof) | Understand what proof claims — and what it does not. | ## Honest claim boundaries Igris does **not** claim universal exactly-once execution against every external system. - External duplicate-effect safety depends on supported idempotent targets. - A Runtime receipt is not proof of external side-effect uniqueness. - Action P

title: Igris Action Protocol
description: Action Protocol Evidence is a separate claim family from managed Runtime execution.
content: Igris Action Protocol Where it sits in the product Practical guidance # Igris Action Protocol The **Igris Action Protocol** is the Evidence family for signed decision and outcome events produced by the SDK journal. It answers questions like: - What Action decision was recorded before execution? - What outcome was recorded after the local/tool path? - Does the local evidence chain verify? It does **not** by itself prove managed control-plane dispatch, Runtime recovery, or external side-effect uniqueness. ## Where it sits in the product text Action Protocol Evidence ≠ Runtime receipt ≠ external effect certainty Igris Run Proof can link these claim families for one durable run while keeping them distinct. See [Igris Run Proof](/docs/igris-run-proof) and [Evidence](/docs/evidence). ## Practical guidance - Use Embedded `wrap_tool` / `@igris.guard` when you want local signed decision/outcome journaling. - Use `IgrisDurableClient` when you want managed durable execution. - Sync and link Evidence explicitly when you need run-scoped eligibility linkage (`igris evidence sync`, then `run.link_evidence`). Protocol remains publicly discoverable here, but first-run onboarding starts with durable Actions, not protocol internals.

title: Actions
description: Actions are typed consequential operations bound to an executable target by exact contract hash.
content: Actions Why exact binding matters Creating targets and bindings Idempotency and targets Related # Actions An **Action** is a typed consequential operation your agent is allowed to run through Igris. In the durable product path, an Action is not “upload this Python function and run it remotely.” It is: 1. an **ActionContract** (name + exact `contract_hash` + parameters) 2. an **Action target** (executable webhook / target identity) 3. an immutable **binding** from exact `contract_hash` → `target_action_id` ## Why exact binding matters Durable runs require the exact `contract_hash`. Binding by Action name alone is rejected. That keeps the executable target pinned to the contract the caller intended, not whatever latest version happens to share a name. ## Creating targets and bindings Use `IgrisDurableClient`: python target = client.create_action_target( name="payments_refund_adapter", target_type="webhook", target_url="https://adapter.example.internal/v1/refund", replay_class="retryable", ) binding = client.ensure_binding( action_name=contract.action_name, contract_hash=contract.contract_hash, target_action_id=target.id, input_mapping= , ) See [Bind an Action](/docs/sdk-bind-action) for the full client surface. ## Idempotency and targets External duplicate-effect safety depends on supported idempotent targets. Igris carries a business idempotency key on the durable run so retries are safe at the Igris layer. That is not the same as every external system being exactly-once. Prefer targets that honor idempotency keys or are otherwise safe under retry. Irreversible targets need extra operational care and may require approval gates. ## Related - [Durable Runs](/docs/durable-runs) - [Business Idempotency](/docs/business-idempotency) - [Your First Durable Action](/docs/first-durable-action)

title: API Reference
description: Customer-facing API guides and endpoint reference for Igris.
content: API Reference Start Here Action Packs Agents Actions Platform Health Inference & Integration Runtime Distribution & Fleet Coordination Account, Trial, and Billing Vault, Policy, and Governance Execution, History, and Receipts Routing Control & Analytics Behavior Trees Durable Tasks MCP Transport Local Runtime API # API Reference This is the customer-facing API contract for Igris. Use the guide pages first, then move into the grouped endpoint reference when you are implementing or debugging a specific route. ## Start Here - [Introduction](/docs/api-reference/introduction) — How the Igris API reference is organized for durable Actions, runs, proof, and MCP. - [Authentication](/docs/api-reference/authentication) — Which credentials belong to automation, browser sessions, and runtime-local deployments, and how to choose the right one for each route. - [Errors](/docs/api-reference/errors) — How to read error responses across the API reference and what to expect from validation, authentication, throttling, and server failures. - [Rate Limits](/docs/api-reference/rate-limits) — What throttling exists today, where it applies, and how clients should behave when they receive a 429 response. ## Action Packs Built-in Action Packs install safe registered actions for first-agent onboarding. A pack is a small manifest of action definitions — it does not execute raw tasks, call external providers, or store secrets. After install, run actions through the normal Actions API or MCP `call_action` like any other registered action. - [`GET /v1/action-packs`](/docs/api-reference/action-packs/get-v1-action-packs) — Lists built-in Action Packs available for install into the authenticated tenant. - [`POST /v1/action-packs/:name/install`](/docs/api-reference/action-packs/post-v1-action-packs-name-install) — Installs a built-in Action Pack by registering its actions in your tenant. Installed actions are normal registered actions — not raw task submissions. ## Agents Tenant-scoped Agent Registry for identity and run attribution. Register an agent before first runs, then pass agent_id or agent_name on action runs and MCP call_action. Metadata is sanitized — no secrets, prompts, or tenant_id from clients. - [`GET /v1/agents`](/docs/api-reference/agents/get-v1-agents) — Lists registered agents for the authenticated tenant. Use include_archived=true to include archived agents. - [`POST /v1/agents`](/docs/api-reference/agents/post-v1-agents) — Registers a tenant-scoped agent identity for run attribution. - [`GET /v1/agents/:id`](/docs/api-reference/agents/get-v1-agents-id) — Gets one registered agent by id. - [`PATCH /v1/agents/:id`](/docs/api-reference/agents/patch-v1-agents-id) — Updates registry f

title: POST /v1/account/api-key
description: Creates a new tenant API key and revokes the old one.
content: POST /v1/account/api-key When To Use Integration Guidance Common Mistakes Related Endpoints Related Guides Code Examples cURL JavaScript Go Rust Sample Response Status Codes 401 Example 500 Example # POST /v1/account/api-key Creates a new tenant API key and returns the raw secret exactly once. The previous key is revoked when the new key is issued, so treat this route as a credential-rotation operation rather than a harmless read/write call. content: POST /v1/actions When To Use Integration Guidance Common Mistakes Related Endpoints Related Guides Request Body Request Example Code Examples cURL JavaScript Go Rust Sample Response Status Codes # POST /v1/actions Creates a registered action definition. The definition declares the execution target, the HTTP method, and the policy that governs every run: preset, replay class, approval requirement, and irreversibility. Once registered, agents run the action by name — they never define execution payloads themselves. Method POST Path /v1/actions Base URL https://overture.igrisinertial.com Auth Session cookie or igris_ API key Surface Cloud API Stability stable Support core Deployment cloud ## When To Use Use this endpoint when setting up a new capability for your agents. Register the action once, then hand agents the action name and an API key. Action names are unique within your tenant. ## Integration Guidance Creation is not idempotent by key, but a retried create with the same name fails safely with `409 action_name_conflict` rather than creating a duplicate. ### Common Mistakes - Forgetting `target_url` for `hosted_api` or `webhook` actions — the action registers, but runs fail with `target_not_configured` until a target is set. - Putting secret values in `secret_refs`. title: POST /v1/actions/:name/run
description: Runs a registered action by name. This is the endpoint agents call in production.
content: POST /v1/actions/:name/run When To Use Integration Guidance Common Mistakes Related Endpoints Related Guides Path Parameters Request Body Request Example Notes Code Examples cURL JavaScript Go Rust Sample Response Status Codes # POST /v1/actions/:name/run Runs a registered action by name inside the authenticated tenant. This is the endpoint agents call in production: one stable URL per action, with policy, tenant-scoped idempotency, runtime routing, recovery, and proof handled by Igris. Only registered actions can run, and tenant identity always comes from your credential, never from the request body. Method POST Path /v1/actions/:name/run Base URL https://overture.igrisinertial.com Auth Session cookie or igris_ API key Surface Cloud API Stability stable Support core Deployment cloud ## When To Use Use this endpoint as the standard way for an agent or service to execute one of your registered actions. Give the agent the action name and a tenant API key; everything else — what the action may do and where it runs — is governed by the registered definition. ## Integration Guidance Send an `idempotency_key` whenever a retry could double-run real work. Retries with the same key inside your tenant return the original run instead of starting a new one. Without a key, treat a timeout as unknown-outcome: inspect recent runs before resubmitting. ### Common Mistakes - Retrying a run without an `idempotency_key` and double-running a side effect that mattered. - Treating a `409 approval_required` response as an error. For human-gated actions it is the expected pause: the run resumes after a reviewer approves it. - Running a `local_runtime` action before a runtime is connected. The gateway refuses with `503 runtime_unavailable` instead of queueing work that cannot execute. ### Related Endpoints - [GET /v1/actions](/docs/api-reference/actions/get-v1-actions) - [POST /v1/actions](/docs/api-reference/actions/post-v1-actions) - [GET /v1/actions/:id](/docs/api-reference/actions/get-v1-actions-id) ### Related Guides - [API Authentication](/docs/api-reference/authentication) - [API Errors](/docs/api-reference/errors) - [Your First Durable Action](/docs/first-durable-action) ## Path Parameters | Field | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `name` | `string` | Yes | Name of the registered action: lowercase letters, digits, underscores, and dots (for example `demo.echo`). | ## Request Body | Field | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `input` | `object` | Yes | Input for this run, passed to the action target. title: POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/approve
description: Approves an action run that is paused awaiting approval and dispatches it for execution.
content: POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/approve When To Use Integration Guidance Common Mistakes Related Endpoints Related Guides Path Parameters Notes Code Examples cURL JavaScript Go Rust Sample Response Status Codes # POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/approve Approves an action run that is paused awaiting approval and continues the controlled action path by dispatching it for execution. A human-gated action returns `409 approval_required` when it is first run; this endpoint is how a reviewer releases that run. Approval is a real gate: the run is only dispatched after this call, tenant ownership is enforced, and a repeated or concurrent approve dispatches the run at most once. Method POST Path /v1/actions/runs/:id/approve Base URL https://overture.igrisinertial.com Auth Session cookie or igris_ API key Surface Cloud API Stability stable Support core Deployment cloud ## When To Use Use this endpoint (or the Approve control in the console) after a run comes back as `approval_required`. Approve when the pending action is within scope for the agent and consistent with your operational policy. Once approved, follow the run with `GET /v1/actions/runs/:id` as you would any other run. ## Integration Guidance Approve is safe to call again. If a runtime was briefly unavailable the run stays in `approval_required` and returns `503 runtime_unavailable`; approve again once a runtime reconnects. Once the run has been approved and dispatched, a second approve returns `409 not_awaiting_approval` instead of dispatching it twice. ### Common Mistakes - Approving a run that is not paused. Only runs in `approval_required` can be approved; anything else returns `409 not_awaiting_approval`. - Expecting a synchronous result. Approve dispatches the run and returns immediately with `status: dispatched`; inspect the run to follow it to completion and proof. ### Related Endpoints - [GET /v1/actions](/docs/api-reference/actions/get-v1-actions) - [POST /v1/actions](/docs/api-reference/actions/post-v1-actions) - [GET /v1/actions/:id](/docs/api-reference/actions/get-v1-actions-id) ### Related Guides - [API Authentication](/docs/api-reference/authentication) - [API Errors](/docs/api-reference/errors) - [Your First Durable Action](/docs/first-durable-action) ## Path Parameters | Field | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `id` | `string` | Yes | Run id returned when the action run was accepted with `approval_required`. | ## Notes - This is the durable action approval route. It approves an action run created through the Actions gateway. title: POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/reject
description: Rejects an action run that is paused awaiting approval. The run is closed and never dispatched.
content: POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/reject When To Use Integration Guidance Common Mistakes Related Endpoints Related Guides Path Parameters Request Body Request Example Notes Code Examples cURL JavaScript Go Rust Sample Response Status Codes # POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/reject Rejects an action run that is paused awaiting approval. A rejected run is closed as a terminal outcome and is never dispatched, so the pending side effect does not happen. Tenant ownership is enforced, and the awaiting-approval precondition is checked atomically so a rejected run cannot later be approved into execution. Method POST Path /v1/actions/runs/:id/reject Base URL https://overture.igrisinertial.com Auth Session cookie or igris_ API key Surface Cloud API Stability stable Support core Deployment cloud ## When To Use Use this endpoint (or the Reject control in the console) when the pending action should not run: it is out of scope, targets the wrong resource, or violates policy. Record a short reason so the decision is clear in the run record. ## Integration Guidance Do not blindly retry write operations. Retry only on transient 5xx or 429 responses, and make sure the client is idempotent or otherwise safe to replay. ### Common Mistakes - Rejecting a run that is not paused. Only runs in `approval_required` can be rejected; anything else returns `409 not_awaiting_approval`. - Expecting a rejected run to resume later. Rejection is terminal. To run the action again, submit a new run through the Actions gateway once the underlying issue is resolved. ### Related Endpoints - [GET /v1/actions](/docs/api-reference/actions/get-v1-actions) - [POST /v1/actions](/docs/api-reference/actions/post-v1-actions) - [GET /v1/actions/:id](/docs/api-reference/actions/get-v1-actions-id) ### Related Guides - [API Authentication](/docs/api-reference/authentication) - [API Errors](/docs/api-reference/errors) - [Your First Durable Action](/docs/first-durable-action) ## Path Parameters | Field | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `id` | `string` | Yes | Run id returned when the action run was accepted with `approval_required`. | ## Request Body | Field | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `reason` | `string` | No | Optional short reason for the rejection, recorded on the run for review. | ## Request Example json { "reason": "target account is out of scope for this agent" } ## Notes - This is the durable action rejection route, paired with `POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/approve`. It is distinct from the older execution-lineage route `POST /v1/execution/runs/:id/reject` on the execution inspection surface. - A rejecte POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/reject Rejects an action run that is paused awaiting approval. The run is closed and never dispatched.

title: API Authentication
description: Authentication models for cloud and local API use.
content: Authentication Tenant API Keys Session Cookies Runtime-local Auth Choosing a Credential Bearer Example Example JSON # Authentication Which credentials belong to automation, browser sessions, and runtime-local deployments, and how to choose the right one for each route. ## Tenant API Keys Customer automation should use tenant API keys with the `igris_` prefix. These keys are the default credential for server-side integrations, CI jobs, backend workers, and any script that is calling the hosted API outside the browser. Supply the key as `Authorization: Bearer ...` or `X-API-Key` if the endpoint allows it. Endpoint pages call out the expected model explicitly, so treat the endpoint page as authoritative over any generic assumption. ## Session Cookies Browser-driven console workflows use session cookies. These routes are designed for an authenticated user session rather than headless automation, so they should not be treated as generic bearer-token endpoints unless the endpoint page says an API key is also accepted. If you are building automation, prefer routes that are documented with API-key access. ## Runtime-local Auth The local runtime API follows the runtime `auth` configuration. Some deployments intentionally keep that surface inside a trusted network boundary with minimal local auth, while others front it with stricter controls. Because that access model depends on deployment, do not assume that a local runtime route behaves like the hosted API. ## Choosing a Credential Use tenant API keys for server-to-server automation. Use session cookies for browser experiences that are already inside the Igris console. Use runtime-local authentication only when the endpoint is explicitly local and you control the deployment boundary. ## Bearer Example text curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $IGRIS_API_KEY" \ https://overture.igrisinertial.com/v1/actions ## Example JSON json { "error": "unauthorized", "code": "INVALID_API_KEY" } API authentication bearer api key session cookie runtime auth

content: GET /v1/tasks/:id When To Use Integration Guidance Common Mistakes Related Endpoints Related Guides Path Parameters Notes Code Examples cURL JavaScript Go Rust Sample Response Status Codes 400 Example 404 Example # GET /v1/tasks/:id Returns the current state of one durable task, including runtime assignment and the latest checkpoint metadata when available. This is the status route you poll while a durable workflow is still in progress. Method GET Path /v1/tasks/:id Base URL https://overture.igrisinertial.com Auth Session cookie or igris_ API key Surface Cloud API Stability stable Support supported Deployment cloud ## When To Use Use this endpoint after submission when you need to monitor progress, completion, failure, or recovery state for a specific task. ## Integration Guidance Safe to retry on transient 5xx or 429 responses. Poll at a reasonable interval rather than continuously, especially for long-running tasks. ### Common Mistakes - Polling too aggressively and turning task status checks into avoidable background load. - Treating checkpoint metadata as if it will exist before the runtime has actually produced a checkpoint. ### Related Endpoints - [POST /v1/tasks/submit](/docs/api-reference/durable-tasks/post-v1-tasks-submit) - [GET /v1/tasks](/docs/api-reference/durable-tasks/get-v1-tasks) - [GET /v1/tasks/:id/steps](/docs/api-reference/durable-tasks/get-v1-tasks-id-steps) ### Related Guides - [API Authentication](/docs/api-reference/authentication) - [API Errors](/docs/api-reference/errors) - [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) ## Path Parameters | Field | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `id` | `string` | Yes | Task ID returned by POST /v1/tasks/submit. | ## Notes - Status values: `pending`, `dispatched`, `checkpointed`, `completed`, `failed`, `recovering`, `approval_required`. - `last_step` and `checkpoint_digest` are only present once the runtime has pushed at least one checkpoint. - Runs created through the Actions gateway also carry optional review fields when they are safely available. They help a person review a run, especially one waiting for approval, and are populated mainly for action-gateway runs; a raw task submission may omit some or all of them. Each is a safe, name-only value that never exposes payloads, request bodies, headers, file contents, secrets, capability scopes, or the run input. - `required_capabilities`: name-only list of the capabilities the run needs, such as `tools.http_request`. Capability names only, never scopes. - `approval_reason`: plain explanation of why the run is waiting for approval. title: API Errors
description: Error handling and common response codes.
content: Errors Status Codes Validation Errors Authentication Failures Server Errors Handling Strategy Error Envelope Example JSON Common Status Codes # Errors How to read error responses across the API reference and what to expect from validation, authentication, throttling, and server failures. ## Status Codes The HTTP status code tells you what class of failure happened before you look at the JSON body. Treat 4xx responses as request, authentication, or access problems that your client should handle directly, and treat 5xx responses as server-side failures that may require retry, fallback, or operator attention. The most common patterns are 400 for invalid request shape, 401 for missing or invalid credentials, 403 for an authenticated request that still is not allowed, 404 when the addressed resource does not exist, 429 when throttling is applied, and 500-level codes when the server cannot complete a valid request. ## Validation Errors Validation failures usually mean the request shape was wrong for the route you called. Many handlers return a compact JSON envelope with `error` and sometimes a more specific `message` or `code` value that tells you what part of the request could not be accepted. ## Authentication Failures Authentication failures typically return HTTP 401. Session-based handlers often use codes such as `MISSING_SESSION` or `INVALID_SESSION`, while API-key handlers more commonly return `INVALID_API_KEY`. ## Server Errors Server-side failures commonly return a generic error such as `internal_error` or a route-specific code such as `registration_failed` or `STORAGE_FAILED`. These responses indicate that the server accepted the route contract but could not complete the operation. ## Handling Strategy Good clients do not handle every error the same way. Fix the request for 400-class validation issues, refresh or replace credentials for 401 responses, stop and inspect authorization assumptions on 403 responses, and apply controlled retry or fallback only for the routes and statuses that are documented as retry-safe. ## Error Envelope text { "error": "invalid_request", "message": "Failed to parse request body" } ## Example JSON json { "error": { "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.", "type": "rate_limit_error", "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED" }, "retry_after_seconds": 60 } ## Common Status Codes | Code | Title | Description | |---|---|---| | 400 | Bad Request | The route was reached, but the request body, query, or path data did not match the endpoint contract. | | 401 | Unauth API errors error codes invalid request unauthorized internal error

title: API Introduction
description: Overview of the customer API contract.
content: Introduction Primary Product Surface How Endpoint Pages Work Recommended First Routes SDK Guidance Support Labels and Deployment Modes Base URLs Example JSON # Introduction How the Igris API reference is organized for durable Actions, runs, proof, and MCP. ## Primary Product Surface Use this API reference after you understand the durable Action journey in [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) and [Your First Durable Action](/docs/first-durable-action). Hosted API calls use `https://overture.igrisinertial.com` with `Authorization: Bearer igris_…`. Prefer the Python `IgrisDurableClient` for application code; use these HTTP contracts when integrating another language or debugging. ## How Endpoint Pages Work Every endpoint has its own page. That page tells you what the route is for, which authentication model it expects, the path and query parameters it accepts, the request body fields that matter, and the status codes you should plan for in a real client. Use the overview page to browse by capability, then switch to endpoint pages when you are implementing or debugging a specific call. ## Recommended First Routes Start with Actions routes: create/inspect targets, create exact contract bindings, submit runs with a business idempotency key and exact `contract_hash`, then inspect runs / Igris Run Proof. Recommended order: `POST /v1/actions`, `POST /v1/contracts/actions/:name/versions/:hash/bindings`, `POST /v1/actions/:name/run`, `GET /v1/actions/runs/:id`. ## SDK Guidance External Alpha first-class SDK support is Python (`igris-sdk`, `IgrisDurableClient`). Other languages should call the hosted Actions HTTP API directly. Some management routes remain direct HTTP integrations. In those cases, the endpoint page is the primary contract. ## Support Labels and Deployment Modes Each endpoint page carries both a support label and a deployment mode. **Core** routes are the primary customer contract. **Supported** routes are part of the shipped product surface but may not be the first endpoint a new customer should start with. **Preview** routes are available, but they should be adopted deliberately. Routes whose stability badge reads **experimental** are disabled by default — they require an explicit experimental feature flag on the deployment and are not part of the stable API contract. Deployment mode tells you where the route belongs operationally. **Cloud** routes are served by the hosted API, **Local** routes are served by local Runtime, and **Hybrid** routes are used when the hosted product and one or more runtimes are working API introduction base URL surfaces overview contract

title: API Rate Limits
description: Rate limit behavior and retry expectations.
content: Rate Limits Global Control-plane Limit Runtime Download Limit Client Behavior 429 Example Example JSON Common Status Codes # Rate Limits What throttling exists today, where it applies, and how clients should behave when they receive a 429 response. ## Global Control-plane Limit The hosted API currently applies a default limiter of 100 requests per minute. Endpoint pages call out the exceptions that matter more than the global default. Response headers are only guaranteed on the 429 path right now. Clients should not assume that every successful response carries full rate-limit metadata. ## Runtime Download Limit Runtime download endpoints use a tighter subscription-aware throttle. Treat binary download as a provisioning or rollout action, not as a hot-path request that your application makes repeatedly during normal traffic. ## Client Behavior Build clients so that a 429 is expected and handled, not treated as an exceptional edge case. Honor `Retry-After` when it is present, apply backoff with jitter for repeated retries, and avoid running parallel request bursts that all wake up at the same second. ## 429 Example text Retry-After: 60 X-RateLimit-Limit: 100 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 ## Example JSON json { "error": { "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.", "type": "rate_limit_error", "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED" }, "retry_after_seconds": 60 } ## Common Status Codes | Code | Title | Description | |---|---|---| | 429 | Too Many Requests | Retry after the advertised cooldown window. | API rate limits retry-after 429 throttle

content: POST /v1/vault/keys When To Use Integration Guidance Common Mistakes Related Endpoints Related Guides Request Body Request Example Code Examples cURL JavaScript Go Rust Sample Response Status Codes 400 Example 401 Example 500 Example # POST /v1/vault/keys Stores a tenant-scoped provider credential for hosted routing. Method POST Path /v1/vault/keys Base URL https://overture.igrisinertial.com Auth Session cookie or igris_ API key Surface Cloud API Stability stable Support supported Deployment cloud ## When To Use Use this endpoint when you are setting up or rotating hosted routing credentials for a tenant. title: Business Idempotency
description: Consequential durable runs require an explicit business idempotency key.
content: Business Idempotency Why it exists How to choose a key What it does not mean Related # Business Idempotency Every consequential durable run requires an explicit **business idempotency key**. The Python durable client never generates a random key for you. That is intentional: retries are only safe when the key names a real business intent (invoice id, transfer request id, change ticket, deploy request, and so on). ## Why it exists Agents retry. Networks flake. Operators re-run scripts. Without a stable business key, a second submit can become a second logical attempt. With the same tenant, Action, contract, and idempotency key, Igris can return the original durable run instead of creating a duplicate logical run. ## How to choose a key Good keys: text refund-cus_8821-2026-07-22 deploy-svc-payments-build-1842 rotate-secret-prod-api-2026-07-22T01 Bad keys: - random UUIDs regenerated on every retry - timestamps that change on every attempt - keys copied from unrelated business events ## What it does not mean Business idempotency at the Igris run layer is **not** universal exactly-once execution against every external system. External duplicate-effect safety still depends on supported idempotent targets. Prefer adapters and backends that honor the same key, or that are otherwise safe under retry. ## Related - [Actions](/docs/actions) - [Durable Runs](/docs/durable-runs) - [Run an Action](/docs/sdk-run-action)

title: Durable Runs
description: A durable run is one contract-bound Action execution you can wait on, recover, and prove.
content: Durable Runs Submit and wait Statuses you should expect What you do not do Related # Durable Runs A **durable run** is one contract-bound Action execution managed by Igris. You submit it once with: - Action name - exact `contract_hash` - input payload - explicit business `idempotency_key` Then you observe it through typed status, wait until terminal (or reconciliation-required), and retrieve **Igris Run Proof**. ## Submit and wait python run = client.run( contract.action_name, input= , idempotency_key="transfer-acct_1-2026-07-22-001", contract_hash=contract.contract_hash, ) status = run.wait(timeout=60.0) proof = run.proof() ## Statuses you should expect Terminal statuses include completed, failed, rejected, cancelled, and unresolved-effect states that require reconciliation. Important product rules: - `recovering` is **not** terminal — keep waiting - unresolved effect states raise `ReconciliationRequiredError` from `wait()` / `status()` by default - the SDK does **not** auto-retry reconciliation-required runs ## What you do not do - Do not manually resume checkpoints in the normal product journey - Do not invent random idempotency keys - Do not treat a successful HTTP accept as proof of the external effect ## Related - [Business Idempotency](/docs/business-idempotency) - [Recovery](/docs/recovery) - [Uncertain Effects](/docs/uncertain-effects) - [Inspect a Run](/docs/sdk-inspect-run)

title: Evidence
description: Evidence is SDK-signed decision/outcome material. Upload and link are explicit.
content: Evidence Sync Link to a run Offline journal verification # Evidence **Evidence** is Action Protocol material: signed decision and outcome events from the SDK journal. Important properties: - Evidence upload is **never automatic** - Linking Evidence to a durable run is a separate eligibility-gated step - Evidence is not proof of managed Runtime execution - `eligible_linked` is server eligibility, not signed run binding ## Sync bash igris evidence sync This uploads journal material to the hosted Evidence surface using `IGRIS_API_URL` and `IGRIS_API_KEY`. ## Link to a run bash igris run link-evidence "$RUN_ID" --batch-id "$BATCH_ID" python link = run.link_evidence(batch_id) print(link.run_linkage_status) If eligibility fails, the client raises `EvidenceNotLinkableError`. ## Offline journal verification bash igris verify igris verify path/to/journal.jsonl --public-key path/to/verify_key.pem See [Verification](/docs/verification) and [Action Protocol](/docs/action-protocol).

title: Your First Durable Action
description: Bind one Action, submit a durable run, wait, and inspect Igris Run Proof.
content: Your First Durable Action Configure the client 1. Declare the consequential function 2. Synchronize the ActionContract 3. Create an Action target 4. Bind exact contract_hash → target 5. Submit one durable run 6. Wait for a terminal status 7. Inspect Igris Run Proof Optional: Evidence sync and link After evidence sync returned a verified batch_id: CLI equivalents Done # Your First Durable Action This walkthrough uses the supported Python durable client: `IgrisDurableClient`. Prerequisites: - External Alpha invitation with API endpoint and `igris_…` API key - `igris-sdk` installed (`pip install ./sdk/python`) - A reachable authenticated webhook Action target for your Action ## Configure the client python import os from igris import IgrisDurableClient, wrap_tool from igris.approval import ApprovalDecision endpoint = os.environ["IGRIS_API_URL"] api_key = os.environ["IGRIS_API_KEY"] client = IgrisDurableClient(endpoint=endpoint, api_key=api_key) ## 1. Declare the consequential function Embedded `wrap_tool` stays local when *you* call it. Durable mode does not upload this Python function to Runtime. The contract is what gets synchronized and bound. python class AlwaysAllow: def decide(self, request): # noqa: ARG002 return ApprovalDecision("allowed", "first durable action") def transfer(account_id: str, amount_cents: int) -> dict: return tool = wrap_tool( transfer, action="demo.consequential_transfer", risk="critical", approval="never", approval_provider=AlwaysAllow(), ) contract = tool.__igris_contract__ print(contract.action_name, contract.contract_hash) ## 2. Synchronize the ActionContract python sync = client.sync_contract(tool) print("synced", sync.contract_hash, "created=", sync.created) ## 3. Create an Action target Register an executable webhook target. Target identity stays visible — this is not Python upload. python target = client.create_action_target( name="demo_transfer_adapter", target_type="webhook", target_url=os.environ.get( "IGRIS_DEMO_TARGET_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:18099/v1/demo/transfer", ), method="POST", replay_class="retryable", approval_required=False, target_metadata={ "local_auth_header_name": "X-Igris-Adapter-Token", "local_auth_secret_env": "IGRIS_DEMO_ADAPTER_TOKEN", }, ) print("target_action_id", target.id) ## 4. Bind exact contract_hash → target Name-only binding is rejected. You must pass the exact `contract_hash` and `target_action_id`. python binding = client.ensure_binding( action_name=contract.action_name, contract_hash=contract.contract_hash, target_action_id=target.id, input_mapping={ "account_id": "account_id", "amount_cents": "amount_cents", }, ) print("binding", binding.id) ## 5. Submit one durable run Provide a stable **business** idempotency key. The client never invents a random one.

title: Igris Run Proof
description: Igris Run Proof links distinct claims for one durable run. It is not one universal cryptographic proof.
content: Igris Run Proof Retrieve it Claim boundaries `eligible_linked` What good use looks like # Igris Run Proof **Igris Run Proof** (`igris_run_proof.v1`) is the product representation returned for a contract-bound durable run. It is a **linked view** of distinct claims for one run. It is not one universal cryptographic proof object, and it does not collapse Runtime receipts with Action Protocol Evidence. ## Retrieve it python proof = run.proof() # prefers igris_run_proof print(proof.schema, proof.product_term) print(proof.statuses) print(proof.claim_boundary) print(proof.runtime_proof) print(proof.action_protocol_evidence) bash igris run proof "$RUN_ID" ## Claim boundaries Read these literally: | Claim | Meaning | |---|---| | Runtime receipt | Managed execution claim. Does **not** prove external side-effect uniqueness or Action Protocol chain validity. | | Action Protocol Evidence | SDK-signed decision/outcome claim. Does **not** prove managed dispatch or Runtime recovery. | | Operator reconciliation | Authenticated operator assertion over unresolved-effect state. **Not** cryptographic proof of the external effect. | | External effect | Neither cryptographic claim independently proves the external effect. | | Linked view | Igris Run Proof joins claims for one durable run; it is not protocol-level cryptographic unification. | ## `eligible_linked` When Evidence is linked to a run, `eligible_linked` means **server eligibility** matched tenant/action/contract/input rules. It is **not** a signed protocol-level run binding, and it is not a universal proof that Evidence and Runtime receipt are one cryptographic object. ## What good use looks like Use Igris Run Proof to answer: - Which Action / contract / binding / business key was this run? - What managed status and recovery lineage does Igris record? - Which distinct proof materials are present or absent? Do not use it to claim “the external world did exactly one thing” unless your target and operational process independently support that conclusion.

title: MCP (Beta)
description: Beta MCP transport for discovering and calling registered Actions.
content: MCP (Beta) Current tool set How to use it in External Alpha Related # MCP (Beta) MCP is a **beta** agent-facing transport for registered Actions. Endpoint: text POST /v1/mcp An agent connects with a tenant credential and can: - discover registered Actions - call a registered Action - inspect resulting runs / evidence surfaces exposed by the tool set - list registered runtimes for the tenant The tool set is fixed and strict-schema (`additionalProperties: false`). Unknown fields are rejected. Tenant identity always comes from the credential. ## Current tool set - `list_actions` - `get_action` - `call_action` - `list_runs` - `get_run` - `get_run_evidence` - `list_runtimes` ## How to use it in External Alpha 1. Complete the durable Action path first with `IgrisDurableClient` so your Action is registered, bound, and runnable. 2. Point your MCP-capable agent at `POST /v1/mcp` on your invitation endpoint. 3. Use tenant API key auth only — never paste raw keys into prompts or shared logs. MCP is secondary to the durable SDK journey. Prefer [Your First Durable Action](/docs/first-durable-action) before MCP wiring. ## Related - [REST API](/docs/rest-api) - [API Reference](/docs/api-reference)

title: Reconciliation
description: Operator reconciliation records an attributable resolution when the external effect is uncertain.
content: Reconciliation When it is required Operator API Application developer rules Related # Reconciliation When a durable run enters an unresolved effect state, Igris requires **operator reconciliation**. This is an attributable administrative assertion over managed unresolved-effect state. It is **not** cryptographic proof of what happened in the external system (`cryptographic_proof: false` on the reconciliation claim). ## When it is required - Run status / recovery state indicates reconciliation is required - `run.wait()` / `run.status()` raises `ReconciliationRequiredError` - Igris Run Proof shows operator reconciliation as needed / present ## Operator API text GET /v1/actions/runs/:id/reconciliation POST /v1/actions/runs/:id/reconciliation `POST` appends an immutable reconciliation event. Typical resolution values: | Resolution | Meaning | |---|---| | `confirmed_succeeded` | Operator confirmed the external effect succeeded | | `confirmed_failed` | Operator confirmed the external effect failed / did not apply | | `remains_unknown` | Operator leaves the effect unknown after inspection | Request shape (conceptual): json { "request_id": "op-recon-2026-07-22-001", "resolution": "confirmed_succeeded", "reason": "Verified transfer id txn_123 in the ledger", "external_reference": { "type": "ledger_transfer_id", "value": "txn_123" } } Reconciliation routes require an authorized operator/admin session for the tenant. They are not a substitute for fixing unsafe application retry loops. ## Application developer rules 1. Catch `ReconciliationRequiredError` 2. Do not auto-retry the durable run 3. Escalate to an operator with access to external system of record 4. After resolution, inspect the run and Igris Run Proof again ## Related - [Uncertain Effects](/docs/uncertain-effects) - [Igris Run Proof](/docs/igris-run-proof) - [Recovery](/docs/recovery)

title: Recovery
description: Infrastructure failures are recovered by the managed durable path — wait and inspect, do not invent resume protocols.
content: Recovery What recovery covers What recovery does not cover Developer pattern Related # Recovery When infrastructure fails mid-run — for example a Runtime host becomes unavailable — Igris can recover the **managed** durable execution. Your job as an application developer is usually: 1. keep the same business idempotency key 2. wait on the run handle (`run.wait()`) 3. inspect status and Igris Run Proof 4. stop if the effect is uncertain You do **not** need a manual checkpoint resume step in the normal SDK journey. ## What recovery covers Recovery covers managed execution continuity for a contract-bound durable run: the control plane and Runtime cooperate so the run can continue after infrastructure replacement or restart. Recovery lineage appears on Igris Run Proof so operators can see that recovery events occurred. ## What recovery does not cover Recovery does not invent certainty about the external world. If the external effect cannot be known safely after a failure, the run enters an unresolved / reconciliation-required state. Automatic retry is unsafe. See [Uncertain Effects](/docs/uncertain-effects). ## Developer pattern python from igris import ReconciliationRequiredError try: status = run.wait(timeout=120.0) except ReconciliationRequiredError as exc: # Inspect the run. Do not auto-retry. print(exc.run_id, exc.recovery_status) raise ## Related - [Durable Runs](/docs/durable-runs) - [Uncertain Effects](/docs/uncertain-effects) - [Reconciliation](/docs/reconciliation) - [Igris Run Proof](/docs/igris-run-proof)

title: Runtime deployment
description: Deploy Runtime so bound Actions can execute against your targets.
content: Runtime deployment What you need for a first durable run Local / operator deployments Application vs operator concerns # Runtime deployment Durable Actions execute through managed Runtime capacity attached to your tenant. For External Alpha, Runtime and the hosted API endpoint are typically provisioned as part of invitation setup. Application developers usually do not need to operate control-plane internals to run their first Action. ## What you need for a first durable run - Hosted API endpoint from your invitation (canonical placeholder: `https://overture.igrisinertial.com`) - Tenant API key (`igris_…`) - At least one healthy Runtime available to your tenant - A reachable Action target (webhook adapter) that the binding points at ## Local / operator deployments If you are operating a Runtime yourself: 1. Install the Runtime binary from your External Alpha kit or release channel 2. Configure the Runtime with the hosted API endpoint and a Runtime credential supplied by Igris 3. Confirm the Runtime registers and remains healthy 4. Keep outbound HTTPS to the hosted API allowed Default local Runtime listen address in many developer setups is `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Application durable calls still go to the **hosted API** endpoint (`IGRIS_API_URL`), not directly to Runtime. ## Application vs operator concerns | Role | Focus | |---|---| | Application developer | `IgrisDurableClient`, bindings, runs, proof | | Operator | Runtime health, network path, reconciliation authority, target adapter availability | See [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting) when runs cannot start because Runtime is unavailable.

title: Bind an Action
description: Synchronize a contract, create a target, and bind by exact contract_hash.
content: Bind an Action 1. Synchronize the contract 2. Create or inspect the target 3. Create or reuse the exact binding CLI Rules # Bind an Action Durable execution requires an exact binding before `run()`. ## 1. Synchronize the contract python sync = client.sync_contract(tool) # or an ActionContract print(sync.action_name, sync.contract_hash, sync.created) ## 2. Create or inspect the target python target = client.create_action_target( name="demo_transfer_adapter", target_type="webhook", target_url="http://127.0.0.1:18099/v1/demo/transfer", method="POST", replay_class="retryable", approval_required=False, ) python existing = client.get_action_target(target.id) ## 3. Create or reuse the exact binding python binding = client.ensure_binding( action_name=contract.action_name, contract_hash=contract.contract_hash, target_action_id=target.id, input_mapping={ "account_id": "account_id", "amount_cents": "amount_cents", }, ) `ensure_binding` returns an existing immutable binding when the target matches, or creates one. If the exact contract is already bound to a different target, it raises `BindingConflictError`. ## CLI bash igris binding create \ --action demo.consequential_transfer \ --contract-hash "$CONTRACT_HASH" \ --target-action-id "$TARGET_ID" \ --input-mapping ' ' \ --json igris binding get \ --action demo.consequential_transfer \ --contract-hash "$CONTRACT_HASH" \ --json ## Rules - `contract_hash` is required (64 lowercase hex) - `target_action_id` is required - `input_mapping` must be a non-empty exact parameter map - consequential bindings require `idempotency_required=True`

title: IgrisDurableClient
description: Construct the explicit durable client with endpoint and API key.
content: IgrisDurableClient Construction Requires BOTH IGRIS_API_URL and IGRIS_API_KEY Authentication Core methods What this client does not do # IgrisDurableClient `IgrisDurableClient` is the supported durable product client. ## Construction python from igris import IgrisDurableClient client = IgrisDurableClient( endpoint="https://overture.igrisinertial.com", api_key="igris_…", ) Or from environment variables — this call is still explicit: python # Requires BOTH IGRIS_API_URL and IGRIS_API_KEY client = IgrisDurableClient.from_env() Partial configuration fails closed. Missing endpoint or API key raises `DurableConfigurationError`. ## Authentication - Credential: tenant-scoped API key (`igris_…`) - Header: `Authorization: Bearer ` - Session cookies are never read or stored by this client Canonical hosted hostname placeholder: text https://overture.igrisinertial.com Use the endpoint from your External Alpha invitation when it differs. ## Core methods | Method | Role | |---|---| | `sync_contract(...)` | Synchronize an ActionContract | | `create_action_target(...)` | Register an executable webhook target | | `ensure_binding(...)` / `create_binding(...)` | Exact `contract_hash` → target binding | | `run(...)` | Submit one durable run | | `get_run(...)` | Fetch typed run status | | `get_proof(...)` | Fetch Igris Run Proof | | `link_evidence(...)` | Link a verified Evidence batch to a run | Run handles returned by `run()` also expose `status()`, `wait()`, `proof()`, and `link_evidence()`. ## What this client does not do - Upload Python source, wheels, pickle, or shell commands to Runtime - Bind by Action name alone - Invent idempotency keys - Auto-retry reconciliation-required states - Collapse Runtime proof and Action Protocol Evidence into one claim

title: Inspect a Run
description: Status, wait, Igris Run Proof, and optional Evidence linking.
content: Inspect a Run Status and wait or Igris Run Proof Evidence link CLI # Inspect a Run ## Status and wait python status = run.status() # or status = run.wait(timeout=60.0, poll_interval=1.0) print(status.status, status.recovery_status, status.is_terminal) `wait()` polls until a terminal status, a reconciliation-required state, or timeout. By default, unresolved effect states raise `ReconciliationRequiredError`. python from igris import ReconciliationRequiredError try: run.wait(timeout=60.0) except ReconciliationRequiredError as exc: print("needs operator reconciliation", exc.run_id, exc.recovery_status) ## Igris Run Proof python proof = run.proof() print(proof.schema) print(proof.claim_boundary) print(proof.statuses) `prefer="igris_run_proof"` is the default. Use `prefer="linked_proof"` only for compatibility with older linked-proof consumers. ## Evidence link Evidence upload remains a separate explicit step (`igris evidence sync`). Linking only attaches an already verified batch: python link = run.link_evidence(batch_id) print(link.run_linkage_status) `eligible_linked` is server eligibility, not signed run binding. ## CLI bash igris run status "$RUN_ID" igris run wait "$RUN_ID" --timeout 60 --json igris run proof "$RUN_ID" igris run link-evidence "$RUN_ID" --batch-id "$BATCH_ID"

title: Troubleshooting
description: Common External Alpha durable Action failures and how to resolve them.
content: Troubleshooting Authentication failures Durable client configuration errors Unbound Action Binding conflicts Missing / conflicting idempotency key Runtime unavailable Wait timeout while recovering Reconciliation required Proof unavailable # Troubleshooting ## Authentication failures **Symptoms:** `AuthenticationError`, HTTP 401. **Checks:** - `IGRIS_API_URL` is exactly the invitation endpoint (no trailing path beyond the host/base) - `IGRIS_API_KEY` is the full `igris_…` secret - The key was not truncated by shell history / secret managers - You are not logging or rewriting the Authorization header ## Durable client configuration errors **Symptoms:** `DurableConfigurationError` on construction or `from_env()`. **Checks:** - Both endpoint and API key are set - You constructed `IgrisDurableClient` explicitly (env alone does not remote Embedded tools) ## Unbound Action **Symptoms:** `UnboundActionError` on `run()`. **Fix:** Create an exact binding with `contract_hash` and `target_action_id` first. See [Bind an Action](/docs/sdk-bind-action). ## Binding conflicts **Symptoms:** `BindingConflictError`. **Meaning:** This exact `contract_hash` is already immutably bound to a different target. Use the existing binding target, or create a new contract version. ## Missing / conflicting idempotency key **Symptoms:** `DurableConfigurationError` (missing key) or `IdempotencyConflictError`. **Fix:** Pass a stable business key. If conflict, inspect the existing run for that key instead of inventing a new one for the same business intent. ## Runtime unavailable **Symptoms:** HTTP 503 / runtime unavailable errors on run submit. **Fix:** Confirm Runtime is registered and healthy for the tenant. See [Runtime deployment](/docs/runtime-deployment). ## Wait timeout while recovering **Symptoms:** `DurableTimeoutError` while status is still non-terminal / recovering. **Fix:** Increase timeout and keep waiting. `recovering` is not terminal. Do not invent a manual resume step. ## Reconciliation required **Symptoms:** `ReconciliationRequiredError`. **Fix:** Do not auto-retry. Follow [Uncertain Effects](/docs/uncertain-effects) and [Reconciliation](/docs/reconciliation). ## Proof unavailable **Symptoms:** `ProofUnavailableError`. **Meaning:** Igris Run Proof is returned for contract-bound durable runs. Unbound or non-bound runs do not carry `igris_run_proof.v1`.

title: Uncertain Effects
description: When the external outcome is unknown, Igris fails closed and requires reconciliation.
content: Uncertain Effects Product rule Why fail closed? What to do next Related claim boundary # Uncertain Effects Some failures leave the external side effect in an **unknown** state: the request may have applied, may not have applied, or may have applied in a way the managed layer cannot safely observe. Igris fails closed in those cases. ## Product rule If a durable run reaches `reconciliation_required` or `unknown_effect_state`: - the SDK raises `ReconciliationRequiredError` from `wait()` / `status()` by default - automatic retry is treated as unsafe - an operator must reconcile with an attributable assertion Do not write application loops that blindly resubmit the Action when the effect is uncertain. ## Why fail closed? Blind retry can double-apply irreversible work. Stopping is the correct default for consequential agents. ## What to do next 1. Inspect the run: `client.get_run(run_id)` or `igris run status "$RUN_ID"` 2. Inspect Igris Run Proof: `run.proof()` / `igris run proof "$RUN_ID"` 3. Check the external system using its own authoritative records 4. Record an operator reconciliation resolution when authorized See [Reconciliation](/docs/reconciliation). ## Related claim boundary Neither Runtime receipt claims nor Action Protocol Evidence independently prove the external effect. Uncertain-effect handling exists because those claims are deliberately separate from “what happened in the outside world.”

title: Evidence
description: Evidence is SDK-signed decision/outcome material. Upload and link are explicit.
content: Evidence Sync Link to a run Verification # Evidence **Evidence** is Action Protocol material: signed decision and outcome events from the SDK journal. Important properties: - Evidence upload is **never automatic** - Linking Evidence to a durable run is a separate eligibility-gated step - Evidence is not proof of managed Runtime execution - `eligible_linked` is server eligibility, not signed run binding ## Sync bash igris evidence sync This uploads journal material to the hosted Evidence surface using `IGRIS_API_URL` and `IGRIS_API_KEY`. ## Link to a run bash igris run link-evidence "$RUN_ID" --batch-id "$BATCH_ID" python link = run.link_evidence(batch_id) print(link.run_linkage_status) If eligibility fails, the client raises `EvidenceNotLinkableError`. ## Verification Offline journal verification remains available: bash igris verify igris verify path/to/journal.jsonl --public-key path/to/verify_key.pem See [Verification](/docs/verification) and [Action Protocol](/docs/action-protocol).
